title: Ekklesia: High-Frequency Voting on Cardano with Hydra

ms.promise:
Due to limited time and development budgets during the initial POC deployments of Ekklesia (during the 2025 Budget Process) we were not able to satisfactorily complete Hydra integration into the platform. During this milestone we will utilize upcoming votes using Ekklesia as a platform to refine and proof Hydra integration in addition to the regular on-chain publication of voting outcome proofs.
Outputs from this milestone will include:
・A report documenting at least one complete voting ballot fully leveraging Hydra on the Cardano Preprod Test Network including:
・Hydra Head opening transaction
・Hydra Head closing transaction
・On-Chain Proof of Ballot Outcomes
・Instructions to fetch and prove the results published on-chain
・Private repository access to relevant source code (to be open sourced pending security audit and needed refactoring in Milestone 4/Final Closeout)
ms.criteria:
To verify that this milestone has been completed the reviewer should be able to:
・Review the Hydra head opening and closing transactions via a publicly available explorer on Preprod test network
・View details of the on-chain ballot proof transaction via a publicly available explorer (Cardanoscan Preprod)
・Use the information published on-chain to download the result proof data
・Follow the instruction to verify that the proof data matches the results in the ballot report
・Review pull requests, commits, and issues related to development of the Ekklesia-Hydra integration within Github repository
ms.report:

Acceptance criteria: A reviewer can open a publicly available Preprod block explorer and inspect the Hydra Head opening sequence (Init, Commit, CollectCom) for the ballot, including the mint of the HydraHeadV1 control token and the participant's commit of the ballot-instance token into the head.

ms.report:
A. Output: Codebase cleanup and audit-preparation work across the four Ekklesia repositories, captured as a v0.9.0 release-candidate cut on the backend and frontend, a public-NPM v1.0.0 release of the shared helpers library, and direct-to-main hardening on the Hydra middleware. The work tightens schemas, deterministic encoding, API versioning, admin/public surface separation, and dependency hygiene so that the codebase is ready for the Milestone #3 security audit.
Acceptance criteria: A reviewer can open each repository, see commits and pull requests against named feature branches identified by the team as the audit-prep release work, and inspect the diff statistics + commit messages that document the cleanup.

Also during this phase we will publish at least one candidate Cardano Improvement Proposal (CIP) to document the various means and mechanisms for utilizing on-chain transactions wherever possible within the Ekklesia platform.
Outputs of this milestone shall include:
・A draft/proposed CIP for on-chain publication of ballot and proposal submissions and Ekklesia results data

ms.report:
Full milestone evidence PDF: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1EIgCFzBWHE87uM-_XdjbF-Ww2MawYxvO/view?usp=sharing
A. Output: A candidate Cardano Improvement Proposal, "Ekklesia - Hydra-Powered L2 Voting Protocol", submitted to the Cardano Foundation CIP repository. The draft specifies the paired CIP-67 token standard (the (600) Ballot Definition and (601) Ballot Instance tokens), the on-chain datum schemas, the voter registration and vote-evidence formats, the merkle-proof auditability system, and the ballot lifecycle, so any future Hydra-based voting application can target the same on-chain primitives.
Acceptance criteria: A reviewer can open the pull request in the official Cardano Foundation CIP repository and read the candidate CIP and its public discussion thread.
Evidence:
・CIP pull request #1207 (cardano-foundation/CIPs): https://github.com/cardano-foundation/CIPs/pull/1207
・Full milestone report (PDF), CIP scope and submission detail in §3: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1EIgCFzBWHE87uM-_XdjbF-Ww2MawYxvO/view?usp=sharing

B. Output: A load testing report for the Hydra middleware vote pipeline. The report benchmarks the pipeline against a realistic mixed voter population at three scale points (10, 100, and 1 000 voters) across the two transaction-submission paths (Direct and TRP), documents the four bottlenecks the first 1 000-voter round exposed, and confirms the improvements in a second round.
Acceptance criteria: A reviewer can open the report and review the harness, methodology, configurations tested, the optimization rounds, and the headline results, with raw run data available on request.
Evidence:
・Load testing report (PDF): https://drive.google.com/file/d/17cxo-rcaVfxridPXQAbjy-s0zC0c1GrB/view?usp=sharing
・Full milestone report (PDF), load testing summary in §4: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1EIgCFzBWHE87uM-_XdjbF-Ww2MawYxvO/view?usp=sharing

ms.promise:
Following the audit of the previous milestone we will perform any development required to remedy identified vulnerabilities and finalize software to a first version formal open source release. As outputs of this milestone we we:
・Release all software as open source under Apache 2.0 licensing
・Release a full release of the software following any necessary development changes to address vulnerabilities in the audit
・Release the findings of the audit as well as remediation steps
・Provide a final closeout report
・Provide a final closeout video
ms.criteria:
In order to accept this milestone as completed the reviewer will be able to:
・Confirm that the source code has been made public and published under an Apache 2.0 software license
・Review the results of the software audit
・Review any remediation steps taken as a result of the software audit
・Review the final closeout report
・Review the final closeout video
ms.report:
A. Output: All Ekklesia software released as open source under the Apache License 2.0. The voting API, the voter web application, the Hydra middleware, the shared cryptographic library, and the documentation site are public repositories on GitHub, each carrying the full Apache License 2.0. The shared library is additionally published to the public npm registry. Complete commit history is preserved rather than squashed, so the remediation of each audit finding can be followed in the record.
Acceptance criteria: A reviewer can open each repository, confirm it is publicly accessible without authentication, and confirm GitHub reports the licence as Apache-2.0.
Evidence:
・Voting API: https://github.com/lerna-labs/ekklesia-backend
・Voter web application: https://github.com/lerna-labs/ekklesia-frontend
・Hydra middleware: https://github.com/lerna-labs/ekklesia-hydra
・Shared library: https://github.com/lerna-labs/ekklesia-helpers
・Documentation: https://github.com/lerna-labs/ekklesia-docs
・Shared library on npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lerna-labs/ekklesia-helpers
・Supporting libraries also released Apache-2.0: https://github.com/lerna-labs/hydra-sdk and https://github.com/lerna-labs/tx3-hydra
・Closeout report, open-source release detail in §3: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XFTmiojlHW5taDEOc6o65ez2t2LtH4jP/view?usp=sharing

B. Output: A full production release of every component, incorporating the development changes required to address the vulnerabilities identified in the security audit. Every representation-changing fix shipped under a bumped protocol version, ekklesia/2.0, with the previous verification path retained, so the two ballots that had already settled on Cardano mainnet before remediation remain verifiable byte for byte on the released code.
